item.group_name: Image edits (the user brings a picture)
item.title: Square Crop Keeps Whole Sneaker

turns.text: Make this wide photo square for an Instagram post. Keep the whole sneaker in view, and don't stretch it or change anything else.

item.tests: Tests converting a 16:9 photo to square while preserving the complete subject and its proportions.

answer_sheet.Subject to preserve: The entire white sneaker, including the toe and heel.
answer_sheet.Style, text and other edits: Keep the original photo appearance. No added text or other edits.

must_haves: The sneaker is the same white leather sneaker as in the attachment.
The entire sneaker, including toe, heel and sole, remains visible.
The sneaker has natural proportions, without stretching or squeezing.
The retained floor and background match the source photo, with no added text or decorative elements.

turns.text: Make this wide sneaker pic square for an Instagram post. Keep the whole sneaker in view, and don't stretch it or change anything else. I'm on the free plan and don't want my credits burned, so tell me what it'll cost before anything runs. Is there a cheaper, shorter, or smaller way to do it?

dialog.agent:
**The cheapest—and safest—option is square padding, not AI editing: 0 Magic Hour credits.** Nothing has run or spent credits.

To keep the whole sneaker and change nothing in the photo:
- Put the original on a square canvas.
- Add equal padding above and below.
- Don’t crop, stretch, or regenerate any pixels.

You can do this free in Canva or another basic image editor. Keep the canvas at the photo’s original width for the smallest file, or export at **1080 × 1080** for Instagram.

With the connected Magic Hour tools, the cheapest AI edit starts at **5 credits** using Flux 2 Klein at **640px** on your free plan. But AI could alter the sneaker or background, so I **don’t recommend it for your exact-preservation request**. Smaller output doesn’t reduce that starting cost; “shorter” only applies to video.

I can’t apply non-AI canvas padding with the tools available here. For the free method, choose a square canvas, center the photo using **Fit**, and use white or gray padding.
dialog.user: ok, go ahead with the cheapest option you listed

turns.agent:
The cheapest option is **0-credit square padding**. I can’t apply that directly with the connected tools, and I won’t substitute a paid AI edit.

For your **512 × 307** photo, use a free image editor to:
1. Create a **512 × 512** canvas with white or gray fill.
2. Place the original photo at its original size, centered.
3. Export as JPG or PNG.

That adds about **102 pixels above and 103 below**, keeping the entire sneaker and every original pixel unchanged. **No credits have been spent.**
